audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this FAVOURED at 4/10 while the level chart hands Nasus levels 6, first item and late, and the Emerald+ win rate is 47.93% over 555 games.
audit.why: A sub-50% matchup that flips to the enemy for the last three stages is not a 4/10 lane; the rating misleads the player into forcing duels after 6.
audit.corrected: diffRating raised to 6/10. The phase sides in the full layer still read Rumble for First item and 2+ items and contradict the content level chart — flagged in notes, not edited, because a 'Rumble'->'Nasus' swap falls outside the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike text explains Fury of the Sands as 'bonus HP and lifesteal' only.
audit.why: Riot's own description says the storm also grants bonus Armor and Magic Resistance and reduces Siphoning Strike's cooldown, and the storm damage is percent-max-HP. Those are the three reasons the stat check actually flips, and none were stated.
audit.corrected: Spike and why rewritten to state percent-max-HP damage, the bonus resists, the Q cooldown reduction, and the 80s vs 130s ultimate cooldown gap.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (R: Fury of the Sands, cd 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Double-tap Electro-Harpoon during his Q animation to cancel his stack' — and the matching line in whys[1] — tells the player a slow cancels Siphoning Strike.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset (autoReset flag, 255 range), not a channel. Electro Harpoon applies damage, a slow and a magic-resist shred; none of those interrupt an attack reset. Following this advice loses both harpoon charges for nothing and denies no stack.
audit.corrected: Both lines rewritten: the harpoon does not cancel the reset, so the denial is positional — hold Flamespitter range over the minion so he must eat the cone to reach 255 range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (E Electro Harpoon: damage, slow, MR shred)

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither is named as the cooldown to track everywhere but its length is never given.
audit.why: 'Track Wither' is unactionable without the number; 15s at rank 1 down to 11s at rank 5 is the whole trading window.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns added to the cooldown breakdown and to whys[1].

audit.why: Liandry's Torment first plus early Oblivion Orb is right against Soul Eater lifesteal and his percent-HP ult.

edits.after: Fury of the Sands is percent-max-HP damage and it hands him bonus armour and MR while cutting his Q cooldown — his 80s ult out-cycles your 130s Equalizer, so stop duelling him.

edits.before: Wither is now online but costs him his only commitment tool — bait it with a fake step-in, then walk into full Flamespitter range and double Electro-Harpoon him off his Q stack animation.
edits.after: Wither is online and it is a 15-second cooldown at rank 1 — bait it with a fake step-in and take the whole trade in that hole. Your harpoon slow will not cancel a Siphoning Strike reset.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands flips the stat check: his bonus HP eats your Flamespitter burst and Wither crumples your movement so you cannot reset — this is now his lane to control.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands flips the stat check: percent-max-HP storm damage, bonus armour and MR, and a shorter Q cooldown, while Wither crumples your movement — this is now his lane to control.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — His only kite. Poke before it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — 15s at rank 1, 11s at rank 5. Poke before it, commit inside it. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: 130s at rank 1 — kill windows only.

edits.before: The Equalizer cuts lanes and teamfights in half — aim it across the path, not on heads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nasus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: The Equalizer cuts lanes and teamfights in half — aim it across the path, not on heads. His R is percent-max-HP and gives him resists, so reassess every all-in at 6.

notes: Nasus's Fury of the Sands GRANTS him bonus armour and magic resist (Riot description) — the _missing-interactions entry 'Nasus bypasses stacking resistances (Fury of the Sands)' is worded backwards; what bypasses resistances is the storm's percent-max-HP damage. Layer conflict left unfixed: full.phases[5].side and full.phases[6].side read 'Rumble' but content.win[5] and win[6] read 'Nasus'; swapping the word breaks the +/-10% length band, so the applier would reject it — needs a manual flip. Nothing verified about Wither being cleansable, tenacity-reduced, or Flash-buffered; the kit file marks all of that unknown and no claim was made.
